title: Sort LL
stepTitle: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
category: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
pattern: merge sort on a linked list
problemStatement: Sort a linked list in O(n log n) time and O(1) extra space.
intuition: Quicksort needs random access; merge sort does not. On a linked list merging is pointer rewiring, so merge sort is the natural choice and needs no auxiliary array.

approaches.title: Brute: copy values, sort, write back
approaches.idea: Easy but uses O(n) memory and ignores the data structure.
approaches.code:
def sort_list_values(head):
    vals = []
    cur = head
    while cur:
        vals.append(cur.val)
        cur = cur.next
    vals.sort()
    cur = head
    for v in vals:
        cur.val = v
        cur = cur.next
    return head

approaches.title: Optimal: top-down merge sort
approaches.idea: Split at the middle with slow/fast, sort both halves, merge.
approaches.spaceNote: O(1) auxiliary data; the log n is recursion depth (bottom-up merge sort removes even that)
approaches.dryRun: 4->2->1->3 splits into (4->2) and (1->3); each sorts; merging gives 1->2->3->4
approaches.whyWorks: Merging two sorted lists is a pointer splice, so no extra array is ever needed.

commonMistakes: Starting fast at head instead of head.next, which fails to split a 2-node list and loops forever
Forgetting slow.next = None to cut the halves apart
patternRecognition: Linked list + O(n log n) -> merge sort, never quicksort
followUps: Bottom-up merge sort for true O(1) space
